name: invitation-panel
title: Invitation Panel
description: InvitationPanel: an admin creates an invitation and gets a one-time link, shown once with a copy button, a live expiry countdown that switches to expired, and a revoke behind a confirmation; below, the pending invitations with role, creator, expiry and revoke, through DataState. Agents can create, copy and revoke, and never read the link.
docs:
`<InvitationPanel aria-label="Invitations" roles={[{ value: "editor", label: "Editor" }]} invitations={pending} status={status} onRetry={refetch} onCreate={({ role }) => api.invite(role)} onRevoke={(id) => api.revoke(id)} text={{ create: "Create invitation", newLink: "New invitation link", expiresIn: (time) => <>Expires {time}</>, createdBy: (name) => `Created by ${name}`, … }} />`.

**The link is shown once.** `onCreate` resolves to `{ id, url, expiresAt }`, and the URL appears in one place only: the new link view, right after it resolves. The panel keeps it in memory, out of its state, and forgets it when the view is dismissed, when the link is revoked or expires, and when the panel unmounts. It never writes it to the address, storage, a `data-*` attribute, a `title` or any `aria-*` text. The pending list's `Invitation` type has no `url`, so your API never has to hand a link out again: a lost link is revoked and a new one created. Keep the URL out of your own logs and state too.

**Agents never read it.** The URL sits under `data-agent-hidden`, so it is left out of the agent snapshot, `query` and every `act` result, and announcements only say a link was created or copied. Agents see the new link in the panel's state as `link: { id, expiresAt, expired }`. `create(role?)` takes a role's value or label and resolves to `{ id, expiresAt }`; `copy()` writes the URL to the clipboard and resolves to `"copied"`. UI SDK's bridge doesn't wait for a promise, so an agent's step reports both as `pending` and reads `link` and `copied` from the next snapshot. `copy` fails with why when no fresh link is held (dismissed, expired, revoked) or the page has no clipboard. `revoke(id)` opens the confirmation for a pending invitation or the new link; its confirm button carries `data-agent-confirm` (`text.revokeAgentConfirm`), so the revoke waits for a person, and an unknown id fails the step. The pending invitations are the panel's agent items, by id.

The countdown is a RelativeTime that ticks by the second in the last two minutes. Expiry takes one timeout per boundary, none while the page is hidden, and checks the clock when the page shows again. The pending list's loading, empty and error states come from DataState (`status`, `error`, and `onRetry` with `text.retry`). Every visible word comes from `text`, with no default; `labels` holds the screen-reader names and announcements, in English by default.

**Invitee fields.** Pass `fields` (FormFields named in `schema`, like a name and an email), with `schema` and `defaultValues`, and the create row becomes a Form: create (the button, Enter in a field, or an agent's `create`) validates them first and shows errors on each field, then calls `onCreate({ role, values })` with the schema's parsed output, typed (`InvitationRequest<z.output<typeof schema>>`). Without `fields`, `values` is `undefined`. A `sensitive` field among them stays out of the DOM and is emptied once the link is created; the fields reset after each link. With fields, an agent's `create` submits the form and returns `true`: the link shows once they pass, and otherwise their errors show on the fields, where the agent reads them.

**Failures.** When `onCreate` rejects with a string or a React node, the live destructive alert shows it as it is ("An account with this email already exists."); a `FormServerError` shows its message there and its field errors on the fields; anything else shows `text.createError`, which can also be a function of the error to pick a message per failure.

**Revoke names.** Pending rows take an optional `invitee` (a name or an email), display only: it titles the row and names its revoke button ("Revoke invitation for leo@example.com"); without one, the name adds the creator and the expiry in the panel's locale, so two invitations from one admin never share a name (`labels.revokeInvitation({ role, createdBy, invitee, expires })`).
